Chemo- and Regiodivergent Allyl-Propargyl Cross-Coupling
Reactions for the Construction of 1,4-Enallenes and 1,5-Enynes
Huijun Qian+, Gabriel N. Morais+, Katherine E. Colbaugh, Junqi Su, Zili Chen, Zhiping Li,*
Shuming Chen,* and Leiyang Lv*
Abstract: Catalyst-controlled divergent transformations represent a vital strategy for the efficient production of structurally
diverse molecules from the same readily available precursors. Herein, we report the palladium/phosphine-catalyst-driven
chemo- and regiodivergent allyl-propargyl cross-coupling of propargyl carbonates with allyl boronates. Density functional
theory (DFT) calculations reveal that the bidentate phosphine ligand plays a crucial role in determining the relative
favorability of possible reductive elimination modes from the <sup>3</sup>-allyl- <sup>1</sup>-allenyl palladium intermediate species. Specifically,
MeO-BIPHEP facilitates the 1,1--reductive elimination to form the 1,4-enallenes; in contrast, XantPhos favors the
formation of 1,5-enynes through a 3,3--reductive elimination pathway.

powerful and efficient strategy for the selective synthesis

precursors.<sup>[1–4]</sup> In this context, the precise manipulation
of reaction intermediates to regulate product distributions
has become a promising approach for designing structural
diversity and complexity.<sup>[5–8]</sup> This approach depends primarily

fine-tuning of tailor-made the catalyst structure and/or appro-
priate reagents, which has attracted significant attention of
chemists.<sup>[9–11]</sup> For example, the palladium-catalyzed coupling

Results and Discussion
Reaction Optimization
The investigation commenced with the treatment of propar-
gylic carbonate 1a and allyl boronate 2a in the presence of
palladium acetate (5 mol%), phosphine ligand and base in
THF (Table 1). The 1,4-enallene product 3a was obtained in
77% yield, along with 12% yield of the byproduct 4a when
BINAP (L1) was used as the ligand. Further investigation
of various bidentate phosphine ligands, including Tol-BINAP
(L2), SDP (L3), MeO-BIPHEP (L4), GARPHOS (L5),
SEGPHOS (L6), DTBM-SEGPHOS (L7), revealed that L4
was the most effective ligand for the formation of the allene
product, affording 3a in 92% yield with only 4% yield for
4a. Notably, the yield of the byproduct 4a was increased
to 31% when DPEphos (L8) was used. This serendipitous
observation prompted us to explore strategies to enhance the
formation of the 1,5-enyne as the main product through ligand
optimization. Encouragingly, the application of Xantphos
(L9) resulted in a significant increase in yield of 4a to 90%. We
then evaluated a series of Xantphos-type ligands,<sup>[60–62]</sup> includ-
ing SiXantphos (L10), NiXantphos (L11), N-Bn-NiXantphos
(L12), SulfoXantphos (L13), <sup>t</sup>Bu-XantPhos (L14), XantPhos-
Pd-G2 (L15), XantPhos-Pd-G3 (L16), and another Xantphos-
based ligand (L17). With the exception of L17, which did not
facilitate the reaction, all other XantPhos-type ligands effec-
tively generated 4a as the major product. Among them, L9
was still the best ligand in terms of both yield and selectivity.

To further probe the factors underpinning the relative
favorability of some reductive elimination TSs over others,
we generated non-covalent interaction (NCI) plots for all
reductive elimination TSs (Figure 1). The NCI plot of TS-
2b revealed extensive stabilizing π–π stacking interactions
between the substrate’s phenyl substituent and the tricyclic
core of the XantPhos ligand. Similar, albeit less extensive, π–
π stacking interactions were also observed in the NCI plots of
TS-1b and TS-1c. To elucidate the role of dispersion interac-
tions (including attractive π–π stacking) in determining the
order of relative free energies of the reductive elimination
transition states, we compared TS energies calculated with
B3LYP (without dispersion) and B3LYP-D3 (with empirical
dispersion). This kind of comparison has been used to
gauge the contribution of dispersion toward calculated energy
differences.<sup>[63,64]</sup> As Table 5 shows, the B3LYP-D3 values rank
the four TSs in the same order as M06-D3, while the B3LYP
values show significant qualitative disagreement, ranking TS-
2d as the lowest-energy TS and TS-2b as much higher in
energy. These values underline the important role played
by dispersion effects, including π–π stacking interactions,
in stabilizing TS-2b. Energy decomposition analysis (EDA)
performed on TS-2a–d also showed that TS-2b has the
most favorable interaction energy between the Pd-XantPhos
framework and the substrate fragments, including particularly
favorable electrostatic interaction and charge transfer terms
(see Table S15 for details).
Another potential contributing factor to the different
ordering of TS free energies between the MeO-BIPHEP
and XantPhos systems is the steric contours of the ligands.
While XantPhos possesses a relatively flat fused tricyclic
core that can accommodate coordinated substrate fragments
in a variety of different orientations, MeO-BIPHEP has a

protruding toward both flanks of the central P─Pd─P axis

MeO-BIPHEP system experiences more steric pressure at

While these computational investigations results have
revealed important differences in non-covalent interaction
strength and ligand steric profiles, we carefully note that
the regioselectivity of this transformation is also significantly
impacted by factors such as the identity of the leaving group,
some of which (including acetate or chloride anions) were
found to lower the regioselectivity in increased concentrations
(see Tables S13 and S14 for details). Although the relative
free energies of the reductive elimination TSs provide one
plausible explanation for the divergent regioselectivity in
the MeO-BIPHEP and XantPhos systems, further modeling
efforts will be necessary to address the roles played by leaving
group anions in influencing the regioselectivity and provide a
complete mechanistic picture.

Conclusion
In conclusion, we have developed a ligand-dependent chemo-
and regioselective allylation of propargylic carbonates with
allylboronates that allows for the highly selective synthesis of
1,4-enallenes and 1,5-alkynes. DFT calculations showed that
the bidentate phosphine ligands play a critical role in deter-
mining the relative favorability of different reductive elimi-
nation modes from the putative ƞ<sup>3</sup>-allyl-ƞ<sup>1</sup>-allenyl palladium
species. Specifically, MeO-BIPHEP promotes 1,1--reductive
elimination to form the 1,4-enallenes, whereas XantPhos
favors the formation of 1,5-enynes via the 3,3--reductive
elimination pathway. This study provides in-depth insights
into the underlying mechanisms of allylation reactions involv-
ing allenyl-palladium complexes and offers a highly efficient
strategy for chemo- and regiodivergent transformations using
readily available identical starting materials.
